text:
This looks like mid-2020. Unemployment of 13.3% matches May 2020 (published in June). Payrolls averaging -6.5M over three months also fits, since March -1.4M (revised), April -20.7M and May +2.7M average about -6.5M. The fed funds rate near 0.08% and a 10-year yield of 0.64% fit as well.

The market data point to the end of May 2020. Large-cap equity returned +1.4% for the month (May 2020 was about +4.8%, while June was about +2%), and the 3-month return of +20.2% fits the period through May or June. Equity returns of +1.4% in 1m and +20% in 3m with a 6m return of -3% match end of May 2020 better, since the S&P 500 was about -5% over 6 months to May and about -3% to June. Hmm.

The unemployment rate was 13.3% in May 2020 and 11.1% in June. The 10-year yield at end of May was 0.65%. The VIX at end of May was about 27.5, and at end of June about 30.4. The VIX here is 31.78, with a 3m change of -21.76, which implies 53.5 three months earlier. End of March 2020 was 53.5, so this is end of June 2020. Core CPI YoY of 1.24% matches June 2020 (1.2%), and headline CPI of 0.24% also matches June (0.6% in June, 0.1% in May). The unemployment rate may be lagged, so June 2020 is the best fit.

The 1m equity return of +1.4% is not quite the S&P's June 2020 return of about 2%, but it is close enough.
